title_vi: Cookie HTTP hoạt động thế nào?

claims.claim_vi: The source says HTTP is stateless, cookies add state, browsers keep cookies from going to the wrong site, and lists SameSite, Name, Value, Secure, Domain and HttpOnly as the cookie's rules.

Set-Cookie carries a name, a value and attributes; Expires or Max-Age set the lifetime and a cookie with neither is a session cookie deleted when the current session ends, the browser defines when that is, and some browsers use session restoring when restarting, which can make session cookies last indefinitely; Secure cookies are sent only over HTTPS (with a localhost exception); HttpOnly stops JavaScript reading the cookie through document.cookie; Domain and Path limit where it is sent; SameSite takes Strict, Lax or None, None must come with Secure, and a cookie with no SameSite is treated as Lax.
claims.section: Define the lifetime; Restrict access to cookies; Cookie prefixes; Controlling third-party cookies with SameSite
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of the repository.

claims.claim_vi: Observed with a Python server and Chromium 141: a cookie set with HttpOnly was absent from document.cookie but was still sent to the server; cookies without HttpOnly appeared in document.cookie.
claims.verified_by: No external page reports this output; observed by executing the code on the authoring machine. MDN states the HttpOnly rule but not this run.

claims.claim_vi: Observed with Chromium 141, treating 127.0.0.1 and localhost as different sites: on a cross-site link navigation (GET) the SameSite=Lax cookie and a cookie with no SameSite were sent and the SameSite=Strict cookie was not; on a cross-site form POST right after login the SameSite=Lax and Strict cookies were not sent but the cookie with no SameSite was; the same POST 130 seconds after login sent no cookies.
claims.verified_by: No external page reports this output; observed by executing the code on the authoring machine. MDN says a cookie without SameSite is treated as Lax; the temporary difference right after creation was observed here and its cause was not checked against a source.

claims.claim_vi: SameSite=Lax leaves cookies out of cross-site form POSTs but sends them on link navigation; stricter SameSite protects better against forged cross-site requests but breaks flows that need cross-site cookies such as embedded content.
claims.section: Controlling third-party cookies with SameSite; Privacy and tracking
claims.verified_by: MDN describes the three values and notes SameSite helps protect against cross-site request forgery; the trade-off wording is the author's summary.

design_notes_vi: Hai thẻ đầu tả luồng Set-Cookie rồi Cookie; sáu thẻ sau gom các thuộc tính theo việc chúng quyết định (đi tới đâu, khi nào, ai đọc, bao lâu); thẻ cuối nêu nên khai SameSite rõ ràng. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source lists Name and Value as attributes beside SameSite, Secure, Domain and HttpOnly; the lesson separates the cookie's name and value from its attributes and adds Path, Expires and Max-Age from MDN.

MDN says a cookie with no SameSite is treated as Lax; the lesson keeps that but records the difference observed in Chromium 141 right after a cookie is created (single run, cause unknown), and advises declaring SameSite explicitly.
Source's playful wording is not used.
